summary: Nine comment-endorsed discoveries spanning calculators, alternative networking, children's books, strategy games, and nuclear history.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | 4,410 comments | history + run artifact updated

items.name: NerdCalci
items.summary: Offline Android calculator with line-by-line calculations and file-based sessions.
items.why_included: Direct praise highlights a simple scratchpad workflow rather than a neutral calculator comparison.
items.evidence: CarlJW loves NerdCalci and praises its simple, line-by-line, file-based format.

evidence_sources.author: CarlJW
evidence_sources.excerpt: I absolutely love NerdCalci! It's simple and gives the same line by line file-based format.

items.name: Numbat
items.summary: Scientific calculation language with physical units; praised for easy custom-unit definitions.
items.why_included: A user explains a concrete reason for switching: custom units help prevent calculation mistakes.
items.evidence: faldor20 switched from SpeedCrunch to Numbat after surveying alternatives and values defining units on the fly.

evidence_sources.author: faldor20
evidence_sources.excerpt: However after surveying the options a while back I switched to numbat. The main advantage is that it's easy to define your own units on the fly.

items.name: SpeedCrunch
items.summary: Free desktop scientific calculator; a longtime user praises its equation-scratchpad workflow.
items.why_included: The submitted product independently earns explicit, long-term first-hand approval in the comments.
items.evidence: sammy2255 calls SpeedCrunch a beloved, years-long taskbar fixture and a go-to equation scratchpad.

evidence_sources.author: sammy2255
evidence_sources.excerpt: Love speedcrunch it has been sitting on my taskbar for many years always my go-to for quick scratchpad for equations, etc.

items.name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library
items.summary: Free children's book-gifting program, available through participating local partners in supported countries.
items.why_included: A parent gives direct, enthusiastic approval from their family's experience.
items.evidence: talon8635 says their family uses the program and calls it a wonderful service.

evidence_sources.author: talon8635
evidence_sources.excerpt: We use it and my son always screen “Dolly!” When we get to her picture in the back jacket. Wonderful service from one of the best Americans to have ever lived.

items.name: PJ Library
items.summary: Free Jewish children's book program delivering age-appropriate stories to eligible families.
items.why_included: A reply explicitly endorses a named book-gifting alternative rather than merely linking it.
items.evidence: talon8635 calls PJ Library a good service for Jewish-themed books.

evidence_sources.author: talon8635
evidence_sources.excerpt: For jewish themed books, PJ Library is a similar good service

evidence_sources.author: nullwarp

items.name: The Battle for Wesnoth
items.source_story_title: fheroes2: A recreation of Heroes of Might and Magic II game engine
items.summary: Turn-based strategy game praised for terrain, day/night cycles, and tactical advantages.
items.why_included: A nested reply supplies specific, first-hand praise for a concrete alternative game.
items.evidence: pennomi recommends Wesnoth for exploiting situational advantages and calls it exceptionally tactical in their experience.

evidence_sources.author: pennomi
evidence_sources.excerpt: Wesnoth is great if you like games where you have to create and exploit situational advantages. Using advantageous terrain, the day/night cycle, and varied unit types makes it one of the most tactical games I’ve played.
